Tunisia Imposes Temporary Tariff on Imported Electrical Transformers, Impacting Utilities Sector

Tunis, June 14—The Tunisian government has implemented a temporary 22% tariff on imported electrical transformers, citing the need to support domestic manufacturers and ensure energy sector resilience. The measure, which took effect last week without prior notice, has already begun reshaping supply chains for the Electric Utilities industry and sparking concern among sector stakeholders.

According to the Ministry of Industry, the tariff will remain in place for at least six months, pending further review. “This is a necessary step to strengthen our local production capacity and reduce dependency on external suppliers,” said Ministry spokesperson Lassaad Ben Salah in a press briefing. He added that the move was prompted by recent supply disruptions and volatility in international markets.

Electric utilities have reported immediate cost increases and are reassessing capital expenditure plans. “We rely on imported transformers for grid maintenance and expansion projects,” said Amira Fekih, head of procurement at El Nour Utility Group. “The tariff puts significant pressure on our budgets and may delay planned upgrades, especially in rural areas.”

Analysts estimate the tariff could raise annual input costs for utilities by up to 18%. The Tunisian Association for Electric Utilities has called for an urgent dialogue with the government. “While we support local industry, abrupt changes like this risk undermining service reliability and investment,” said the association in a statement.

As the tariff remains in effect, utilities are exploring alternative suppliers within Tunisia and considering postponing non-essential projects until the policy is reviewed.
